newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine working on syndicated credits - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine working on syndicated credits - deputy PM.

text.p: Ukraine is working on a number of syndicated credit projects to prove to foreign investors there are many ways to invest in the former Soviet republic, Serhiy Tyhypko, deputy prime minister in charge of reforms, said on Thursday.
"We are trying jointly with a European bank to realise a mechanism of syndicated credits," he told a news conference.
Four areas for potential credit projects were being considered "to show it is possible to work on state, municipal, banking and enterprise levels," he said.
The first project would involve a credit to the Finance Ministry worth about $150 million, which Ukraine was hoping to receive in two to two and a half months, he added.
Other programmes were being worked on for the city of Kiev, two banks and a pilot project for the Azovstal metallurgical plant in the southern city of Mariupol.

Foreign investment in Ukraine has totalled only $1.5 billion since the country won independence in 1991. Several big companies have pulled out of major projects, complaining of demands for bribes and constantly changing legislation.
